rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding signs, support for God's allies, and humiliation of His enemies establish His unlimited power and knowledge, so praise necessarily belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: ولما أثبت سبحانه بعده بإثبات الآيات المرئية والمسموعة وإعزاز أوليائه وإدلال أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise belongs to God because it encompasses every attribute of perfection, and His perfection belongs to Him intrinsically.
rows.anchor: أثبت أنه لا بالإحسان والتدبير فقال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's lordship over the heavens and earth is not dependent on His beneficence or governance; each domain has distinct secrets and forms of nurture.
rows.anchor: أن له في كل واحد من الخافقين أسرارا غير ما له في الآخر , فالتربية متفاوتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction before Lord of the earth stresses that God's power and lordship are equal over the upper and lower realms, with no distance limiting Him.
rows.anchor: كمال قدرته في ربوبيته للأعلى والأسفل على حد سواء دفعا لتوهم أن حكمه في الأعلى أمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth are named first as conspicuous signs, then all worlds are included: the world is everything besides God, with no creature outside His knowledge or power.
rows.anchor: فجمع ما مفرده يجل على جميع الحوادث لأن العالم ما سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeatedly calling God Lord signals that His preservation and nurture vary with each creature, each part, and the whole, although all are equally within His power.
rows.anchor: حفظه للخلق وتربيته لهم ذو ألوان بحسب شؤون الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone possesses limitless grandeur throughout all the heavens and earth; this underscores His unique sovereignty and answers claims of partners.
rows.anchor: أي الكبر الأعظم الذي لا نهاية له

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة وأبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra (Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah) and Abu Sa'id (Muslim) transmit God's saying that grandeur and greatness are His garments and whoever contests either is cast into the Fire.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم وأبو داود وابن ماجة عن أبي هريرة ومسلم عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report gives variant threats: God may say that He will punish or crush the one who contests His grandeur or greatness.
rows.anchor: وفي رواي : عذبته , وفي رواية : قصمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible and overcomes everything; as the Wise, He places all things perfectly and has perfected His commands, law, and the Qur'an's arrangement.
rows.anchor: الذي يضع الأشياء في أتقن مواضعها ولا يضع شيئا إلا كذلك كما أحكم أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's wording, meaning, and revelation fit the circumstances answered; its ending returns to its opening through God's attributes, His signs, and the grandeur that humbles enemies and honors allies.
rows.anchor: وأحكم نظم هذا القرآن جملا وآيات , وفواصل وغايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described are companions of Paradise, remaining there forever as the recompense for their works.
rows.anchor: صرح بها بقوله تعالى : { خالدين فيها } خلودا لا آخرا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because their deeds are sincerely good and part of their disposition, God makes them causes of reward that continue through their renewed practice.
rows.anchor: ولما كانوا محسنين فكانت أعمالهم في غاية الخلوص جعلها تعالى أسبابا أولا وثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pairs the command to obey Him, the Creator, with kindness to parents, whom He made the means of human creation; prayer on time ranks first and filial kindness second.
rows.anchor: الوصية بالوالدين لكونه تعالى جعله سبب الإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a hadith in al-Tirmidhi that God's approval follows the parents' approval and His displeasure follows theirs.
rows.anchor: وفي الترمذي : ( رضى الله في رضى الوالدين وسخطه في سخطهما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an regularly places kindness to parents after the command to worship God, as in the covenants with Israel and the command not to associate partners with Him.
rows.anchor: القرآن يوصي بطاعة الوالدين بعد الأمر بعبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses humankind as a species, and the implied completion is that a person should treat both parents well.
rows.anchor: أي هذا النوع الذي أنس بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufan reciters read إحسانا, which the author says better fits the context.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون : { إحسانا } وهو أوفق للسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father's visible earning, spending, protection, and discipline are left unstated, while the mother's shorter period of hardship is detailed so it is not undervalued.
rows.anchor: وذكر ما للأم لأن أمده يسير , فربما استهين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother carries and delivers the child with hardship; this establishes her special right and shows that God alone brings the child into being.
rows.anchor: فدل هذا - مع دلالته على وجوب حق الأم - على أن الأمر في تكوينه لله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thirty months are the combined pregnancy and full nursing period; calling it weaning points to its endpoint, since nursing can stop and resume before completion.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالفصال لإرادة النهاية لأن الفطام قد يكون قبل النهاية لغرض ثم تظهر الحاجة فتعاد الرضاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the full term totals thirty months, the minimum pregnancy is six months; doctors agree, and the calculation may imply a minimum nursing period of one year and nine months if pregnancy usually lasts nine months.
rows.anchor: فانصرف الفصال إلى الكامل الذي تقدم في البقرة فعرف أن أقل مدة الحمل ستة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction extends through a stage when parents may share the burden or one may bear it alone; the verse divides people into obedient and disobedient, with glad tidings and warning for each.
rows.anchor: ذاكرا ما لكل من الجزاء بشارة ونذارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines al-ashudd as strength, variously locating it from eighteen to thirty and explaining its unusual plural-like form through several competing morphological analyses.
rows.anchor: قوته , وهو ما بين ثماني عشرة سنة إلى ثلاثين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-ashudd is age thirty-three, the age at which Jesus son of Mary was raised.
rows.anchor: أنه قال : الأشد ثلاث وثلاثون سنة , وهو الذي رفع عليه عيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: الهيثمي
rows.claim: Al-Haythami says the report's chain contains Sadaqa ibn Yazid, whom Abu Zur'a and Abu Hatim trust while Ahmad and others weaken; its remaining narrators are reliable.
rows.anchor: قال الهيثمي : وفيه صدقة بن يزيد وثقه أبو زرعة وأبو حاتم وضعفه أحمد وجماعة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari places the beginning of al-ashudd at maturity and its endpoint at forty.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : وهو أول الأشد وغايته الأربعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At forty a person's strength, resolve, and seriousness are complete and youthful rashness subsides; this is why prophets were commissioned at that age, and childhood and the years before forty carry lighter accountability.
rows.anchor: فاجتمع أشده وتم حزمه وجده , وزالت عنه شرة الشباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Youth's pleasures often conceal life's purpose as base appetites and anger dominate; reaching forty signals the loss of that ease and the need to reflect.
rows.anchor: لغلبة الأنفس الخبيثة عليه البهيمية والسبعية لما يحملانه عليه من نتائج الشهوات ونوازع الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awzi'ni asks God to make the speaker able and steadfast in gratitude, restraining him so that he never lets gratitude be overcome.
rows.anchor: { أوزعني } أي اجعلني أطيق { أن أشكر نعمتك } أي وازعا للشكر أي كافا مرتبطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude for God's blessing means worshipping Him alone; the singular blessing magnifies the difficulty, since even one blessing cannot be repaid without divine help, while the mention of parents indicates the whole class of blessings.
rows.anchor: وذلك الشكر بالتوحيد في العبادة كما أنه يوحد بنعمة الإيجاد والترزيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer names blessings actually bestowed on the speaker, personally due to his special claim, and on his parents through existence and bodily health; their blessing is also his.
rows.anchor: أي بالفعل لوجوب ذلك علي لخصوصه بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest past blessing is existence, whose proper gratitude is monotheism, so the prayer adds the further request to perform righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: المقصود الأعظم من النعمة الماضية نعمة الإيجاد المراد من شكرها التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deed may be righteous in itself yet fail to be acceptable without God's authorization; the indefinite wording acknowledges that no one can give God His full due.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الصالح في نفسه قد يقع الموقع لعدم الإذن فيه قال : { ترضاه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After teaching prayer for oneself and one's parents, God teaches prayer for descendants so they will not be empowered to disobey; their righteousness benefits the parent and should be firmly rooted among them.
rows.anchor: لقنه سبحانه الدعاء لمن يتفرع منه , حثا على رعاية حقوقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At forty, a person may see most of life as wasted; repentance is a condition for accepted prayer and means returning from everything that impairs turning to God.
rows.anchor: علله بقوله : { إني تبت } أي رجعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic declaration of repentance and being among Muslims reflects how difficult it can be to abandon desires and submit outwardly and inwardly with complete obedience.
rows.anchor: وأكده إعلاما بأن حاله في الإقبال على الشهوات حال من يبعد منه الإقلاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage generalizes from this believer to humankind and says their best deeds are accepted; respect for parents is a condition of accepted worship because outward conduct reveals the inner state.
rows.anchor: منبها على أن قبول الطاعات مشروط ببر الوالدين لأن ما ظهر دليل ما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that one who does not thank people has not thanked God; the point especially applies to parents, among the closest and most causally important people.
rows.anchor: كما في الحديث ( لا يشكر الله من لا يشكر الناس )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound relationship with God repairs relations with people generally and especially with relatives and parents.
rows.anchor: ومن صلح ما بينه وبني الله صلح ما بينه وبين الناس عامة لا سيما الأقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural divine verb presents acceptance as gracious and effortless, while its form suggests God attends carefully to accepting the deeds.
rows.anchor: { الذين نتقبل } بأسهل وجه { عنهم }

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read both verbs in the first-person plural, “We accept” and “We overlook.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص بالنون فيه وفي الذي بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The best of what they did” may mean prayer or acts of obedience; deeds below the highest may also be accepted according to intention, and the wording “from them” implies continuing ascent toward perfection.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد به مطلق الدعاء أو الطاعات ويكون ما دون الأحسن مقبولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises to overlook their sins; the accepted promise is certain, and this reading means they will not be reproached for them.
rows.anchor: { عن سيئاتهم } أي فلا يعابهم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does this for them while they are counted among Paradise's companions, since they have always remained under His favor.
rows.anchor: { في أصحاب الجنة } أي أنه فعل بهم ذلك وهم في عدادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is true because it matches reality, and the messengers had continually promised it in worldly life.
rows.anchor: { وعد الصدق } لكونه مطابقا للواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what people conceal, especially when it contradicts their public claims, and exposes the hypocrites; this continues the discussion of those who listen to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: علم ما أبطنه الإنسان ولا سيما إن كان مخالفا لما أظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those called believers include both sincere people and hypocrites; their request for revelation can signal sincere desire for the Qur'an, the true spirit, to renew their worship and action.
rows.anchor: أي ادعوا ذلك بألسنتهم وفيهم الصادق والمنافق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction reflects their belief that revelation comes only from God, so they need not name its source; they request any surah to recite and follow, with successive revelation invigorating them.
rows.anchor: وبناه للمفعول دالة على إظهار أنهم صاروا في صدقهم في الإيمان اعتقادهم أن التنزيل لا يكون إلا من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A surah means any complete portion of the Qur'an, whether revealed gradually or all at once; the revealed surah exceeds the request by being decisive and containing fighting.
rows.anchor: أي قطعة من القرآن تكامل نزولها كلها تدريجا أو جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A decisive surah is clear, without ambiguity or abrogation, because it gathers what is excellent for every time and place.
rows.anchor: مبينة لا يلبس شيء منها بنوع إجمال ولا ينسخ لكونه جامعا للمحاسن في كل زمان ومكان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits from Qatada that every surah mentioning jihad is decisive and that such passages are the hardest part of the Qur'an for hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وهو مروي عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' spiritual sickness means either weakness in religion or hypocrisy; these are people who had professed belief and asked for revelation.
rows.anchor: أي ضعف في الدين أو نفاق من الذين أقروا بالإيمان وطلبوا تنزيل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had sworn emphatically that they would go out if ordered, but they look at the Prophet with loathing once fighting is revealed.
rows.anchor: وكانوا قد أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fixed, unblinking gaze resembles someone fainting at death and expresses cowardly aversion to fighting.
rows.anchor: { من الموت } الذي هو نهاية الغشي فهو لا يطرف بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most interpreters treat awla as the comparative pattern, whose root sense of turning or inclination yields intensified misery; the author understands it as a threat of ruin.
rows.anchor: على صيغة أفعل التفضيل - وهو قول الأكثر - جاءت الشدة

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i parses awla as a past-tense verb: destruction has drawn near to them and God has plunged them into ruin.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي : إنه فعل ماض أي قاربهم ما يهلكهم

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Radi calls awla a proper name of threat, marked by a verb pattern and therefore diptote; he rejects the comparative and verbal-noun parses, citing Abu Zayd's feminine form أولاة.
rows.anchor: وقال الرضي في باب المعرفة والنكرة : إنه علم للوعيد وفيه وزن الفعل فلذا منع من الصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the hypocrites' discourteous words and bad conduct, obedience and proper speech would serve them better than professed love masking aversion.
rows.anchor: أي بالتسليم والإذعان وحسن الانقياد خير لهم مما أظهروا من المحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite nouns allow obedience and decent speech to mean either their highest forms or any degree of them.
rows.anchor: ونكر الاسمين ليكونا صالحين للتعظيم وما دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the order to fight or another command is firmly decided, truthful obedience to God would be better than evading it.
rows.anchor: فإذا أمر بالقتال الذي ذكر في أول السورة وغيره من الأوامر أمرا مجزوما به معزوما عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr may be read as a non-comparative noun, making explicit that their lying to God is evil for them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( خير ) اسما لا للتفضيل ليفهم أن كذبهم شر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke turns into direct address and a rhetorical question to show that God's anger has reached its limit and to expose the ruin caused by their hesitation.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على تناهي الغضب وبلوغه الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They eagerly requested revelation, but when God mercifully commands what is best, namely fighting, they may hate and flee; they should fear the corruption their own behavior predicts.
rows.anchor: أي فتسبب عن تسرعكم إلى السؤال في أن يأمركم الملك بما يرضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional inserted between عسيتم and its predicate presents turning away from God's command as resistance to sound human nature and reason.
rows.anchor: فصل بين ( عسى ) وخبرها بشرطية معبر فيها بالتولي بصيغة التفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active reading means that they themselves turn away from fighting; in the passive reading reported by Ruways from Yaqub, someone causes and adorns their desertion.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى الثاني هو المراد ببنائه للمجهول في رواية رويس عن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their land corruption would be grave, sustained, hateful warfare; whoever is too cowardly to do what pleases God for the afterlife may dare what angers Him for worldly desire.
rows.anchor: بقتال يكرهه الله ويسخطه ويغضب أشد غضب على فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their pre-Islamic raids on one another already exemplified the corruption that comes from turning away from God's commands.
rows.anchor: وقد كنتم في الجاهلية على ذلك في الغارة من بعضكم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Severing kin would leave believers unsupported, possibly let enemies defeat them, and deprive the deserters of their relatives' benefits; killing or belatedly avenging them compounds the loss.
rows.anchor: وأقل ما في إعراضكم خذلانكم للمؤمنين المجاهدين بما قد يكون سببا لظهور الكافرين عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining right and fighting wrong protects society from corruption and severed kinship, while abandoning that duty brings both.
rows.anchor: وقد علم من هذا أن من أمر بالمعروف وجاهد أهل المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse may mean gaining political authority; it then foretells rule by wicked people and warns against neglecting enjoining right, whose corrupting results were witnessed.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون ( توليتم ) من ولاية الأمر , فتكون الآية مشيرة إلى ولاية الفجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose, reflected in its name, includes the Hudaybiyya truce, the conquest of Mecca and Khaybar, and other victories, as well as the Romans' victory over Persia.
rows.anchor: مقصودها مدلول اسمها الذي يعم فتح مكة وما تقدمه من صلح الحديبية وفتح خيبر ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan conquest led to Arabia's conversion, the wars against apostasy, and the conquest of lands, all culminating in the triumph of the true religion.
rows.anchor: وما تفرع من فتح مكة المشرفة من إسلام أهل جزيرة العرب وقتال أهل الردة وفتوح جميع البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah itself displays this purpose from its promise that the religion will prevail through its account of Muhammad and its mention of victories that anger the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: بما نطق ابتداؤها { ليظهر على الدين كله } { محمد رسول الله } إلى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of forgiveness for believers echoes the surah's opening promise to the Messenger; the great reward also covers later victories and their spoils.
rows.anchor: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوةا الصالحات منهم مغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, God is the all-powerful and all-knowing King; the Merciful extends the promise and warning to all accountable people, while the Compassionate singles out His party to establish true religion and prevail.
rows.anchor: الملك الأعظم المحيط بكل شيء قدرة وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding surah on fighting, this surah announces victory to the fighters; as with al-Nasr following al-Kafirun, the previous surah's conclusion makes this opening victory inevitable.
rows.anchor: لما كانت تلك سورة الجهاد وكانت هذه سورة محمد بشارة للمجاهدين من أهل هذا الدين بالفوز والنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous surah described disbelievers' destruction and believers' guidance, urged continued struggle, promised support and firm footing, and warned that deserters would be replaced by people who would not retreat.
rows.anchor: وختمها بالتحريض على مجاهدتهم بعد أن ضمن لمن نصره منهم النصر وتثبيت الأقدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That pattern guarantees the abasement of disbelief and elevation of faith, which is the manifest victory; the opening states it as a certain conclusion, affirming it for the virtuous and refuting the many whose hearts were sick.
rows.anchor: فكان ذلك محتما لسفول الكفر وعلو الإيمان , وذلك بعينه هو الفتح المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's majesty makes the victory certain; the past tense presents its causes as fully established and the result as already accomplished.
rows.anchor: { فتحنا } أي أوقعنا الفتح المناسب لعظمتنا لكل متعلق بإتقان الأباب المنتجة له من غير شك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victory benefits the Prophet by elevating God's word and filling the earth with security; each good deed earns its doer a like reward, and the community will comprise two-thirds of Paradise's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: فلا يعمل منهم أحد حسنة إلا كان له مثل أجرها ويكونون على قصر زمنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening victory was the Hudaybiyya treaty in Dhu al-Qa'da of year six; this surah was revealed concerning that event as the Muslims returned to Medina.
rows.anchor: أي بصلح الحديبية في ذي القعدة سنة ست من الهجرة التي نزلت هذه السورة في شأنه

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says no victory was greater than the Hudaybiyya peace, because mingling with Muslims let the polytheists hear their words and see their unmatched character.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري : لم يكن فتح أعظم من صلح الحديبية , وذلك أن المشركين اختلطا بالمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victory also includes vindication of the report that the Romans would defeat the Persians, for those who date that victory to the Hudaybiyya period.
rows.anchor: وكذا كان من الفتح تقوية أمره صلى الله عليه وسلم بالتصديق فيما أنزل عليه من سورة من غلبهم على أهل فارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victory is manifest because no reasonable person could miss that Muhammad would prevail over the world after beginning alone, with a handful of weak, persecuted followers.
rows.anchor: أي لا لبس فيه على أحد , بل يعلم كل ذي عقل به أنك ظاهر على جميع أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After thirteen years of persecution in Mecca, God rescued the followers through migration to the Negus and then Medina, protected Muhammad from assassination, and frustrated efforts to stop his emigration or bring him back.
rows.anchor: ثم أنقذ الله أتباعك منهم بالهجرة إلى النجاشي رحمه الله تعالى أولا , وإلى المدينة الشريفة ثانيا
